topics.name: Job: overview
topics.description: Job opens with a righteous man losing everything (1-2), moves through his lament and long exchanges with three friends (3-31), Elihu (32-37) and the LORD answering from the whirlwind (38-41), and ends with Job’s repentance and restoration (42).
evidence: Outline the book of Job in its main parts: prologue, speeches, the LORD’s answer, epilogue.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline the book of Job in four or five parts and name who speaks in each?

topics.name: Job’s integrity and the loss of everything
topics.description: Job is described as blameless and God-fearing and is very rich; the LORD allows Satan to take his possessions and children, and Job worships, saying the LORD gave and the LORD has taken away.
evidence: Retell what Job lost in chapter 1 and how he responded (1:20-22).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Job in chapter 1 and what he said when he heard the news?

topics.name: Job’s sores and his friends’ silence
topics.description: Satan is allowed to strike Job’s body with sore boils, his wife tells him to curse God and die, Job refuses, and three friends come and sit with him seven days without speaking.
evidence: Explain how Job answers his wife in 2:9-10 and what the three friends do in 2:11-13.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Job says to his wife and what his three friends do when they arrive?

topics.name: Job laments the day of his birth
topics.description: Job breaks the silence by cursing the day he was born and asking why light is given to those in misery who long for death.
evidence: Summarize Job’s complaint in chapter 3 and name what he wishes had happened (3:11-13).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Job speaks in chapter 3 and how it differs from his words in chapters 1-2?

topics.name: Eliphaz’s first speech
topics.description: Eliphaz says the innocent do not perish and those who sow wickedness reap it, tells of a night vision asking whether mortal man can be more just than God, and urges Job to seek God and not despise his correction.
evidence: Identify Eliphaz’s argument in 4:7-8 and his advice in 5:8 and 5:17.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} state Eliphaz’s main argument to Job in chapters 4-5?

topics.name: Job answers: my grief is heavy, my friends fail me
topics.description: Job says his grief outweighs the sand of the sea, compares his friends to a stream that fails in summer, and cries that his days are hopeless and short, asking God why he is watched so closely.
evidence: Find the image Job uses for his friends in 6:15-20.
Describe how Job speaks to God in 7:11-21.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Job answers Eliphaz in chapters 6-7 and what he asks of God?

topics.name: Bildad’s first speech
topics.description: Bildad asks whether God perverts justice, suggests Job’s children sinned, and says that if Job is pure God will restore him while the hope of the godless perishes.
evidence: Note Bildad’s questions in 8:3 and the promise in 8:20-21.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Bildad says about God’s justice and what he thinks it means for Job?

topics.name: How can a man be right with God? Job longs for a mediator
topics.description: Job agrees that a man cannot contend with a God of great power, laments that there is no daysman between them to lay a hand on both, and in chapter 10 pleads with God to show why he contends with him, recalling that God made him.
evidence: Find Job’s question in 9:2 and his wish in 9:33.
List what Job says about being made by God in 10:8-12.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Job means by wanting a daysman in 9:33?

topics.name: Zophar’s first speech
topics.description: Zophar accuses Job of empty talk, says God’s wisdom cannot be searched out, and promises that if Job puts away iniquity and prepares his heart he will be secure, while the eyes of the wicked fail.
evidence: What does Zophar say about searching out God (11:7-9) and about repentance (11:13-19)?
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} summarize Zophar’s first speech and compare it with Bildad’s?

topics.name: Job replies: God’s power, and whether a man will live again
topics.description: Job tells the friends he is not inferior to them, says wisdom and strength belong to God, who overturns counsellors and kings, declares he will trust God though he slay him, and in chapter 14 asks whether a man who dies shall live again.
evidence: Locate 13:15 and 14:14 and say what each expresses.
List things God does to rulers in 12:17-21.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Job speaks of God’s power in chapter 12 and what he asks about death in 14:14?

topics.name: Eliphaz’s second speech: the wicked man’s torment
topics.description: Eliphaz rebukes Job for vain words and describes at length how the wicked man suffers pain and fear all his days.
evidence: Describe the picture of the wicked man in 15:20-35.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Eliphaz accuses Job of in chapter 15 and how he describes the wicked?

topics.name: Job: miserable comforters, and a witness on high
topics.description: Job calls his friends miserable comforters, says God has broken and worn him down, yet declares that his prayer is pure and that his witness is in heaven; his spirit is broken and the grave is ready for him.
evidence: Find the phrase Job uses for his friends in 16:2 and what he claims in 16:17-19.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Job describes his friends and what he says about a witness in chapters 16-17?

topics.name: Bildad’s second speech: the light of the wicked is put out
topics.description: Bildad describes the wicked man snared, terrified and rooted out of his tent so that his remembrance perishes from the earth.
evidence: List the images of the wicked man’s end in chapter 18.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list two of the pictures Bildad uses for the end of the wicked?

topics.name: I know that my redeemer lives
topics.description: Job says God has fenced his way and his family and friends have forsaken him, and he longs for his words to be written, declaring that he knows his redeemer lives and that in his flesh he shall see God.
evidence: Read 19:23-27 and state what Job says he knows and expects to see.
List the losses Job names in 19:13-20.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Job 19:25-27 and say what Job expects in spite of his condition?

topics.name: Zophar’s second speech: the triumph of the wicked is short
topics.description: Zophar says the triumphing of the wicked is short, that ill-gotten riches will be vomited up, and that God casts the fury of his wrath on him.
evidence: State Zophar’s claim in 20:5 and the portion he assigns the wicked in 20:29.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Zophar’s claim about the wicked in chapter 20?

topics.name: Job: the wicked often prosper
topics.description: Job answers that the wicked live, grow old, see their children established and die at ease, and asks how often the lamp of the wicked is put out, rejecting his friends’ consolations as falsehood.
evidence: Find where Job describes the wicked at ease in 21:7-13 and contrast it with the friends’ claims.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Job’s words in chapter 21 challenge the friends’ view of the wicked?

topics.name: Eliphaz’s third speech: accusation and a call to return
topics.description: Eliphaz asks whether a man can profit God, accuses Job of specific wrongs against the poor, and calls him to return to the Almighty and be built up.
evidence: List the charges Eliphaz makes in 22:5-9 and the invitation in 22:21-30.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Eliphaz now accuses Job of and what he tells him to do?

topics.name: Job: I cannot find him, yet he knows my way
topics.description: Job longs to come to God’s seat and plead his case but cannot find him forward or backward; he says God knows the way he takes and that when tried he shall come forth as gold, and chapter 24 asks why the oppression of the poor goes unpunished.
evidence: Find 23:3-10 and say what Job wants and what he is confident of in 23:10.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what Job wants from God in chapter 23 and what troubles him in chapter 24?

topics.name: Bildad’s short speech and Job’s reply
topics.description: Bildad says dominion and fear are with God and asks how man can be clean before him; Job replies by describing God’s power over the deep and the heavens and swears he will hold fast his integrity until he dies.
evidence: Compare the length of Bildad’s speech (ch. 25) with Job’s answers (26-27).
Find Job’s vow in 27:2-6.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Job vows in chapter 27 and why he refuses to agree with his friends?

topics.name: Where shall wisdom be found?
topics.description: Job describes how men mine silver and gold from the earth, yet wisdom cannot be found in the deep or bought with gold; God alone knows its place, and tells man that the fear of the LORD is wisdom and to depart from evil is understanding.
evidence: Contrast what men can find by mining (28:1-11) with what they cannot (28:12-22).
State the answer in 28:28.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Job 28:28 and explain how it answers the question asked in 28:12 and 28:20?

topics.name: Job remembers his former honour and describes his shame
topics.description: Job recalls the months when God preserved him, when he was honoured and delivered the poor, then describes being mocked by those younger, with God not hearing his cry.
evidence: Contrast Job’s life in chapter 29 with chapter 30.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} compare Job’s condition in chapter 29 with his condition in chapter 30?

topics.name: Job’s oath of innocence
topics.description: Job lists wrongs he says he has not done, from lust and falsehood to neglecting the poor, the fatherless and the stranger, trusting gold, and rejoicing at an enemy’s fall, and desires that the Almighty answer him; the words of Job end.
evidence: Choose three of Job’s denials in chapter 31 and say which commands of right conduct each shows.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name three kinds of wrong Job says he has avoided in chapter 31?

topics.name: Elihu speaks: anger at Job and the three
topics.description: The three men stop answering because Job is righteous in his own eyes; Elihu, younger than they, is angry with Job for justifying himself and with the friends for finding no answer, and says the Spirit within man gives understanding.
evidence: Name why Elihu was angry with Job and with the three friends (32:2-3).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Elihu speaks and why he waited?

topics.name: Elihu: God speaks, and sends an interpreter
topics.description: Elihu says God speaks to man in dreams and by suffering to turn him from pride, and that if there is a messenger, an interpreter, to show man his uprightness, God is gracious and ransoms him.
evidence: Find 33:14-30 and list the ways Elihu says God speaks to and restores a person.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list two ways Elihu says God speaks to men in chapter 33?

topics.name: Elihu: God does no wickedness
topics.description: Elihu says God will not do wickedly or pervert judgment and rewards each man according to his work, rebukes Job for saying it profits nothing to delight in God, and says God sees but does not owe man.
evidence: Find the sentence in 34:10 and the charge against Job in 34:35-37.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} state what Elihu says about God’s justice in chapter 34?

topics.name: Elihu: the greatness of God in the storm
topics.description: Elihu says God is mighty, teaches through affliction, and is beyond understanding; he describes God’s command over rain, lightning and thunder and tells Job to stand still and consider God’s wondrous works.
evidence: List the weather phenomena Elihu names in 36:27-37:13.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name three works of God Elihu points to in chapters 36-37?

topics.name: The LORD answers Job out of the whirlwind: creation and the animals
topics.description: The LORD answers Job out of the whirlwind with questions about the foundations of the earth, the sea, light, rain, the stars, and the lion, raven, wild goat, wild ass, ostrich, horse and hawk, none of which Job made or controls.
evidence: Pick five of the LORD’s questions in chapter 38 and say what each says about God’s power.
List the animals in chapter 39.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD is showing Job by asking questions about creation in chapters 38-39?

topics.name: Job lays his hand on his mouth
topics.description: The LORD asks whether the faultfinder will instruct the Almighty and challenges Job to answer; Job says he is vile and will not answer again, and the LORD calls him to gird up his loins and asks whether he will condemn God to justify himself.
evidence: Compare Job’s first reply (40:3-5) with the LORD’s second challenge (40:6-14).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Job responds in 40:3-5 and what the LORD asks next?

topics.name: Behemoth and Leviathan
topics.description: The LORD describes behemoth, which he made, as chief of his ways with great strength, and leviathan, which no man can hook, tame or stand before; he asks who can stand before him and says all under heaven is his.
evidence: Name what the LORD says in 41:10-11 about standing before the creature and before him.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD speaks of behemoth and leviathan to Job?

topics.name: Job sees God and repents
topics.description: Job says he knows God can do everything, that he spoke of things too wonderful for him, that he had heard of God by the ear but now his eye sees him, and he abhors himself and repents in dust and ashes.
evidence: Say what Job confesses in 42:2-6 and what changed for him from hearing to seeing.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Job 42:1-6 and describe what Job confesses?

topics.name: The LORD restores Job and rebukes the friends
topics.description: The LORD says the three friends have not spoken of him rightly as Job has, tells them to offer a burnt offering with Job praying for them, and then gives Job twice as much as before, seven sons and three daughters, and many more years.
evidence: State why the LORD is angry with Eliphaz and his friends (42:7).
List what the LORD gives Job in 42:10-16.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells the friends to do, and what happens to Job at the end?

topics.name: Psalms: overview
topics.description: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
evidence: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?

topics.name: Psalm 1: the blessed man and the way of the ungodly
topics.description: The blessed man delights in the law of the LORD and is like a tree by streams of water, while the ungodly are like chaff and their way shall perish.
evidence: Contrast the tree and the chaff in Psalm 1 and say what each picture shows.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the two ways in Psalm 1 and what the blessed man delights in?

topics.name: Psalm 2: the nations rage, the LORD’s king is set on Zion
topics.description: The kings of the earth set themselves against the LORD and his anointed, the LORD laughs and says he has set his king on Zion, declares him his Son, and warns the kings to serve the LORD with fear.
evidence: List who rages against whom (2:1-3), who answers (2:4-6), and what the kings are told to do (2:10-12).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline Psalm 2 in its four parts and say what the kings are warned to do?

topics.name: Psalms 3-4: trusting the LORD and sleeping in peace
topics.description: In Psalm 3 many rise up against the speaker but the LORD is a shield and he lies down and sleeps; in Psalm 4 he asks the LORD to hear him, says the LORD has put gladness in his heart, and lies down in peace.
evidence: Find the verse about sleep in each psalm (3:5, 4:8) and say what gives the speaker peace.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how the speaker of Psalms 3 and 4 is able to sleep despite trouble?

topics.name: Psalms 5-7: prayers for help against enemies and for the LORD’s judgment
topics.description: Psalm 5 is a morning prayer to a God who hates wickedness, Psalm 6 is a weary cry for mercy and healing, and Psalm 7 appeals to the LORD as righteous judge to save the speaker from persecutors.
evidence: Find the request in 5:8, the groaning in 6:6, and the appeal to God’s judgment in 7:8-9.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how each of Psalms 5, 6 and 7 begins and what the speaker asks?

topics.name: Psalm 8: what is man? the LORD’s majesty and man’s place
topics.description: The speaker praises the LORD’s excellent name, considers the heavens, the moon and stars, and asks what man is that God remembers him, saying God made him a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory, with dominion over the works of his hands.
evidence: Read 8:3-8 and list what is put under man’s dominion.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Psalm 8:3-6 and say what it teaches about God and man?

topics.name: Psalms 9-10: the LORD is a refuge for the oppressed and judges the wicked
topics.description: Psalm 9 praises the LORD who sits on his throne judging, is a refuge for the oppressed and does not forget the cry of the humble; Psalm 10 asks why he stands afar and describes the wicked who persecute the poor, ending with the LORD hearing the humble.
evidence: List what the wicked say and do in Psalm 10:2-11, and the LORD’s response in 10:16-18.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalms 9 and 10 speak of the LORD as judge of the oppressor?

topics.name: Psalms 11-12: refuge when the faithful fail
topics.description: Psalm 11 says the LORD is in his holy temple and trieth the righteous, and the speaker trusts him instead of fleeing; Psalm 12 says the godly cease and men speak flattery, but the words of the LORD are pure and he will arise for the poor.
evidence: Read 11:1-4 and 12:5-6 and say why the speaker trusts the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the speakers of Psalms 11 and 12 trust the LORD when evil seems strong?

topics.name: Psalm 13: how long, O LORD?
topics.description: The speaker asks how long the LORD will forget him and hide his face, pleads for light lest his enemy rejoice, and ends by trusting in the LORD’s mercy and singing.
evidence: Trace how the psalm moves from “how long” in 13:1-2 to singing in 13:5-6.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 13 moves from complaint to trust?

topics.name: Psalms 14 and 53: the fool says there is no God
topics.description: Both psalms say the fool has said in his heart there is no God, that the LORD looked down from heaven to see if any seek him, and that all are gone aside and none does good; the psalms end with a longing for the salvation of Israel.
evidence: Compare Psalm 14:1-3 and 53:1-3 and note the repeated words.
Find the closing wish in 14:7 and 53:6.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} compare Psalms 14 and 53 and say what they teach about human beings?

topics.name: Psalm 15: who may dwell in the LORD’s tabernacle?
topics.description: Asked who may abide in the LORD’s tabernacle and dwell in his holy hill, the psalm answers with the one who walks uprightly, speaks truth, does not slander or take usury or bribes, and honours those who fear the LORD.
evidence: List the qualities named in 15:2-5.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list four qualities of the person described in Psalm 15?

topics.name: Psalm 16: the LORD is my portion and I will not be moved
topics.description: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD, calls him his portion and cup, sets him always before him, and expects his heart to be glad and his soul not left in hell, with fulness of joy and pleasures at God’s right hand.
evidence: Read 16:5-11 and list the reasons the speaker rejoices.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 16:8-11 about the LORD’s presence?

topics.name: Psalm 17: hide me under the shadow of thy wings
topics.description: The speaker appeals to the LORD to hear his right, says his heart has been tried and found without fault, asks to be kept as the apple of the eye from violent men, and expects to behold God’s face and be satisfied.
evidence: Read 17:8-9 and 17:15 and say what the speaker asks and expects.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the two pictures of God’s care in Psalm 17:8?

topics.name: Psalm 18: the LORD my rock and deliverer; a king’s thanksgiving
topics.description: The speaker loves the LORD as rock, fortress and deliverer, describes God coming down in storm and fire to rescue him from death and strong enemies, and gives thanks for strength in battle and for deliverance given to his king and anointed.
evidence: Read 18:1-6, 18:30-36 and 18:50 and list who delivers and who is delivered.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 18 pictures the LORD rescuing the speaker?

topics.name: Psalm 19: the heavens declare God’s glory, and his law is perfect
topics.description: The heavens declare the glory of God day and night to all the earth, and the law, testimony, statutes and judgments of the LORD are perfect, sure, right and sweeter than honey; the speaker asks to be cleansed from secret and presumptuous sins.
evidence: Read 19:1-6 and 19:7-11 and say what each half says about God.
Read 19:12-14 as a prayer.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how God makes himself known in Psalm 19 through the heavens and through his law?

topics.name: Psalms 20-21: prayer and thanksgiving for the king
topics.description: Psalm 20 prays that the LORD hear the king in the day of trouble and says some trust in chariots but we remember the name of the LORD; Psalm 21 thanks the LORD that the king rejoices in his salvation, with his heart’s desire and a crown.
evidence: Read 20:7 and 21:7 and say whom the king trusts.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the contrast in Psalm 20:7 and who the king trusts in Psalm 21?

topics.name: Psalm 22: my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
topics.description: The speaker cries to God who seems far, is scorned and surrounded by enemies, his bones out of joint and garments divided, then declares God’s name in the congregation and says all the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the LORD.
evidence: Read 22:1-21 and list the pictures of suffering.
Read 22:22-31 and say how the psalm ends.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 22 moves from the opening cry to the closing praise?

topics.name: Psalm 23: the LORD is my shepherd
topics.description: The LORD is the speaker’s shepherd who leads him to green pastures and still waters, restores his soul, is with him in the valley of the shadow of death, prepares a table before enemies, and goodness and mercy follow him to the house of the LORD forever.
evidence: List what the shepherd does in each verse of Psalm 23.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD does for the speaker in Psalm 23 and where the psalm ends?

topics.name: Psalm 24: the King of glory
topics.description: The earth is the LORD’s and all in it; those with clean hands and a pure heart may ascend his hill, and the gates are told to lift up their heads for the King of glory, the LORD of hosts.
evidence: Read 24:3-6 and say who may ascend, and 24:7-10 and say who comes in.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain who may stand in the LORD’s holy place and who the King of glory is in Psalm 24?

topics.name: Psalm 25: teach me thy ways; forgive my sin
topics.description: The speaker lifts up his soul to the LORD, asks to be taught his ways and truth, asks him not to remember his youthful sins and to pardon his great iniquity, and says the LORD teaches the meek and sinners in the way.
evidence: Read 25:4-11 and list what the speaker asks for.
Read 25:8-14 and say whom the LORD teaches.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list what the speaker asks for in Psalm 25 and whom the LORD teaches?

topics.name: Psalm 26: examine me; I walk in my integrity
topics.description: The speaker asks the LORD to judge and test him, says he walks in his truth, has not sat with vain persons, loves the LORD’s house, and asks not to be gathered with sinners.
evidence: List what the speaker says he has done and not done in 26:3-8.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks God to do in Psalm 26:1-2?

topics.name: Psalm 27: the LORD is my light and salvation
topics.description: The speaker says the LORD is his light, salvation and strength, so he will not fear though an army encamp against him; he desires to dwell in the LORD’s house, seeks his face, and says to wait on the LORD.
evidence: Read 27:1-6 and 27:13-14 and state what the speaker is confident about.
Read 27:4 and say what he most desires.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the speaker of Psalm 27 does not fear and what he asks for in 27:4?

topics.name: Psalms 28-29: the LORD my strength; the voice of the LORD
topics.description: Psalm 28 is a cry to the LORD the rock, then blessing him because he has heard and is the speaker’s strength and shield; Psalm 29 summons the mighty to give glory to the LORD whose voice is over the waters and shakes the wilderness, and who gives strength to his people.
evidence: Find 28:7-8 and 29:11 and note how both speak of the LORD’s strength to his people.
List what the voice of the LORD does in 29:3-9.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list three things the voice of the LORD does in Psalm 29?

topics.name: Psalm 30: weeping may endure for a night
topics.description: The speaker extols the LORD who lifted him up and healed him from the grave, says the LORD’s anger endures a moment but his favour is life, and that mourning was turned into dancing.
evidence: Read 30:5 and 30:11-12 and say what changed.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 30:5 says about weeping and joy?

topics.name: Psalm 31: into thine hand I commit my spirit
topics.description: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD as rock and fortress, commits his spirit into his hand, describes distress, reproach and fear on every side, says his times are in the LORD’s hand, and blesses him for his goodness laid up for those who fear him.
evidence: Read 31:5, 31:15 and 31:19 and state what each says about trusting the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what it means that “my times are in thy hand” in Psalm 31:15?

topics.name: Psalm 32: blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven
topics.description: The speaker says the one whose transgression is forgiven is blessed, describes bones wasting while he kept silent about his sin, and says that when he acknowledged his sin to the LORD he was forgiven and now the LORD is his hiding place.
evidence: Contrast 32:3-4 with 32:5.
Read 32:1-2 and note who is called blessed.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens in Psalm 32:5 when the speaker confesses his sin?

topics.name: Psalm 33: sing to the LORD who made all things by his word
topics.description: The righteous are called to sing to the LORD a new song because his word is right and by his word the heavens were made; he looks on all men, brings counsel of nations to nought, and his eye is on those who fear him and hope in his mercy.
evidence: Read 33:6-9 and 33:16-19 and say how God’s word and rescue are described.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 33:6-9 says about creation by the LORD’s word?

topics.name: Psalm 34: taste and see that the LORD is good
topics.description: The speaker blesses the LORD at all times, tells how this poor man cried and the LORD saved him, says the angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, teaches children the fear of the LORD, and says the LORD is near the broken-hearted.
evidence: Read 34:1-10 and 34:11-14 and list what the speaker teaches the children.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Psalm 34 teaches about crying to the LORD and what children are taught in 34:11-14?

topics.name: Psalm 35: plead my cause against false accusers
topics.description: The speaker asks the LORD to contend with those who strive with him, to let the angel of the LORD chase them, and describes false witnesses who repay evil for good; he promises thanks in the great congregation.
evidence: Read 35:7, 35:11-12 and 35:18 and describe the wrong done to the speaker.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the wrong done to the speaker in Psalm 35 and what he asks of the LORD?

topics.name: Psalm 36: the wicked and the fountain of life
topics.description: The transgression of the wicked says there is no fear of God before his eyes, while the LORD’s mercy reaches to the heavens and his faithfulness to the clouds; with him is the fountain of life and in his light we see light.
evidence: Contrast 36:1-4 with 36:5-9.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast what Psalm 36 says about the wicked and about the LORD?

topics.name: Psalm 37: fret not, trust in the LORD
topics.description: The psalm tells the reader not to fret over evildoers but to trust in the LORD, delight in him, commit his way to him and wait; the wicked will be cut off and the meek shall inherit the earth.
evidence: Read 37:1-9 and list the commands given.
Read 37:25 and say what the speaker has observed.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list three commands in Psalm 37:1-8 and what is promised to the meek?

topics.name: Psalm 38: a penitent’s cry in suffering
topics.description: The speaker asks the LORD not to rebuke him in wrath, says his flesh and bones suffer because of his sin and iniquity, his friends stand aloof and enemies speak against him, yet he hopes in the LORD and confesses his iniquity.
evidence: Read 38:1-4 and 38:15-18 and say what the speaker confesses and hopes.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the speaker of Psalm 38 connects his suffering to his sin and what he does about it?

topics.name: Psalm 39: make me to know my end
topics.description: The speaker resolves to guard his tongue, asks the LORD to make him know his end and how short his days are, calls man’s life an handbreadth, says his hope is in the LORD, and asks to be spared.
evidence: Read 39:4-7 and say what the speaker asks and what he concludes about his hope.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks God to teach him in Psalm 39:4-7?

topics.name: Psalm 40: I waited patiently for the LORD
topics.description: The speaker waited patiently for the LORD who lifted him from a pit and put a new song in his mouth, says the LORD desires obedience and not sacrifice and offering, declares his righteousness to the congregation, and asks for help as poor and needy.
evidence: Read 40:1-3 and 40:6-8 and say what the LORD desires according to the speaker.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 40:6-8 about sacrifice and the LORD’s will?

topics.name: Psalm 41: blessed is he that considers the poor
topics.description: The one who considers the poor is blessed and the LORD delivers him in trouble; the speaker, ill and slandered by enemies and even a familiar friend, asks for mercy and the psalm ends with a blessing on the LORD.
evidence: Read 41:1-3 and 41:9-13 and say who is blessed and who betrays the speaker.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what blessing Psalm 41:1-3 gives to the one who considers the poor?

topics.name: Psalms 42-43: my soul thirsts for God; why art thou cast down?
topics.description: The speaker pants after God like a deer after water, remembers going to God’s house, and three times asks his soul why it is cast down and tells it to hope in God; Psalm 43 asks God to plead his cause and lead him to his holy hill.
evidence: Find the repeated refrain (42:5, 42:11, 43:5) and say how the speaker answers his own soul.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read the refrain of Psalms 42-43 and say what the speaker tells his soul?

topics.name: Psalm 44: a lament of God’s people after defeat
topics.description: The people recall what God did for their fathers in giving the land, say they trust not in their bow, but now God has cast them off, scattered them and made them a reproach though they have not forgotten him, and they ask him to awake and redeem them.
evidence: Read 44:1-8, 44:9-16 and 44:17-26 and say what each section says.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the people complain in Psalm 44 and what they ask?

topics.name: Psalm 45: a song for the king
topics.description: The speaker addresses a king who is fairer than the sons of men, whose throne is for ever and whose sceptre is righteous; he is anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows, and a king’s daughter is brought to him.
evidence: Read 45:1-7 and say what is said about the king and 45:10-15 about the bride.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how the king and his throne are praised in Psalm 45?

topics.name: Psalm 46: God is our refuge and strength
topics.description: God is a very present help in trouble, so the speakers will not fear though the earth is removed and the waters roar; God is in the midst of the city, the LORD of hosts is with us, and he makes wars cease and says, Be still, and know that I am God.
evidence: Read 46:1-3, 46:4-7 and 46:8-11 and find the refrain in 46:7 and 46:11.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 46:10 asks and why the speakers do not fear?

topics.name: Psalms 47-48: God is king over all the earth; the city of God
topics.description: Psalm 47 calls all peoples to clap and shout for God, who is the great King over all the earth; Psalm 48 praises the LORD in the city of our God on the mountain of Zion, where God is known as a refuge.
evidence: Find 47:2, 47:7-8 and 48:1-3 and say what is said about God’s kingship and Zion.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalms 47 and 48 say about God as king and about Zion?

topics.name: Psalm 49: no man can redeem his brother; God will redeem my soul
topics.description: The speaker calls all peoples to hear his wisdom and says those who trust in wealth cannot redeem a brother or give God a ransom, men die like beasts and carry nothing away, but God will redeem his soul from the grave.
evidence: Read 49:6-9 and 49:15 and contrast what riches cannot do with what God does.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says about riches and death in Psalm 49 and what he says God will do?

topics.name: Psalm 50: God judges his people; offer thanksgiving
topics.description: God speaks from Zion to gather his saints who made a covenant with him by sacrifice, says he does not need bulls and goats, tells them to offer thanksgiving and call on him in trouble, and rebukes the wicked who hate instruction.
evidence: Read 50:7-15 and 50:16-23 and say what God asks and what he rebukes.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what God says in Psalm 50:9-15 about sacrifice and thanksgiving?

topics.name: Psalm 51: have mercy upon me, O God
topics.description: The speaker pleads for mercy and cleansing, confesses his transgression and says he sinned against God only, asks for a clean heart and a right spirit and that God not take his holy spirit, and says God desires a broken and contrite heart.
evidence: Read 51:1-4 and say what the speaker confesses.
Read 51:10-17 and list what he asks and what God accepts.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Psalm 51:10-12 and say what the speaker asks God to do?

topics.name: Psalms 52 and 54: God against the deceitful and violent
topics.description: Psalm 52 asks why the mighty man boasts in mischief, says God will destroy the deceitful tongue, and compares the speaker to a green olive tree trusting in God’s mercy; Psalm 54 asks God to save him from strangers and oppressors and says God is his helper.
evidence: Compare what the boaster trusts (52:7) with what the speaker trusts (52:8).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast the man in Psalm 52:7 with the speaker in 52:8?

topics.name: Psalm 55: betrayed by an equal, cast thy burden on the LORD
topics.description: The speaker is overwhelmed by fear and wishes he had wings to flee, sees violence in the city, is wounded not by an enemy but by an equal and familiar friend, and resolves to pray evening, morning and noon, trusting that God will hear.
evidence: Read 55:12-14 and 55:16-22 and say who wounds the speaker and what he does.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker does in Psalm 55:16-17 and who has caused his grief in 55:12-14?

topics.name: Psalms 56-57: in God I will trust and not be afraid
topics.description: In Psalm 56 the speaker says that when afraid he will trust in God and not fear what man can do; in Psalm 57 he takes refuge in the shadow of God’s wings and says his heart is fixed to sing, asking God to be exalted above the heavens.
evidence: Find 56:3-4, 56:11 and 57:1, 57:7 and say what the speaker does when afraid.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker does when afraid in Psalm 56:3-4?

topics.name: Psalms 58-59: God judges unjust rulers and rescues from violent men
topics.description: Psalm 58 asks whether the congregation judges uprightly and appeals to God to break the teeth of the wicked, concluding that there is a God who judges in the earth; Psalm 59 asks God to deliver from bloodthirsty enemies and sings of his strength and mercy.
evidence: Read 58:11 and 59:16-17 and say how each psalm ends.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalms 58 and 59 end and what each says about God?

topics.name: Psalm 60: a prayer after a defeat
topics.description: The speaker says God has cast off and scattered his people and made them drink the wine of astonishment, prays for deliverance, recalls God’s claim on Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim and Judah, and says vain is the help of man while through God we shall do valiantly.
evidence: Read 60:1-5 and 60:11-12 and say what the people ask and trust.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 60:11-12 says about help from man and from God?

topics.name: Psalms 61-62: my rock and my refuge; wait on God alone
topics.description: In Psalm 61 the speaker cries from the end of the earth and asks to be led to a rock higher than he, a strong tower; in Psalm 62 his soul waits on God alone, his rock and salvation, and he says power belongs to God and mercy belongs to him.
evidence: Find 61:2-3 and 62:1-2, 62:5-8 and list the names for God.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list the names for God in Psalm 62:1-8 and say what the speaker does?

topics.name: Psalm 63: my soul thirsts for thee
topics.description: The speaker earnestly seeks God in a dry and thirsty land, says God’s lovingkindness is better than life, remembers him on his bed in the night watches, and says his soul follows hard after God and the king shall rejoice in God.
evidence: Read 63:1-8 and list the ways the speaker seeks and praises God.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 63:3 says about God’s lovingkindness?

topics.name: Psalm 64: hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked
topics.description: The speaker asks God to preserve his life from enemies who sharpen their tongues like swords and shoot bitter words and plan snares in secret; God shall shoot at them and all men shall fear and declare his work.
evidence: Read 64:3-6 and 64:7-10 and contrast the wicked’s weapons with God’s.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the wicked do and what God does in Psalm 64?

topics.name: Psalms 65-67: praise for God’s forgiveness, creation and blessing of the nations
topics.description: Psalm 65 says praise waits for God who purges transgressions and waters the earth and crowns the year with goodness; Psalm 66 calls all lands to praise him for his works and for bringing his people through trial; Psalm 67 asks God to bless us so that all the earth may fear him.
evidence: Find 65:3, 65:9-13, 66:5-12 and 67:1-3 and list what is praised.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the refrain of Psalm 67:3 and 67:5 asks of all the peoples?

topics.name: Psalm 68: let God arise
topics.description: The psalm begins with Let God arise and his enemies be scattered, calls God a father of the fatherless and judge of the widows who leads his people, and calls the kingdoms of the earth to sing to God who rides on the heavens.
evidence: Read 68:1-6 and 68:32-35 and note who is called to rejoice and sing.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 68:5-6 says about God’s care for the weak?

topics.name: Psalm 69: zeal for thy house; they gave me vinegar
topics.description: The speaker is sinking in deep waters and hated without cause, says zeal for God’s house has consumed him and reproaches have fallen on him, that he was given gall and vinegar, asks that his adversaries’ table be a snare and their eyes darkened, and ends with praise.
evidence: Read 69:1-4, 69:9, 69:21 and 69:22-28 and list what the speaker suffers and asks.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the suffering in Psalm 69:1-4 and 69:20-21 and how the psalm ends?

topics.name: Psalms 70-71: make haste to help; forsake me not in old age
topics.description: Psalm 70 is a short cry for God to hasten and help the poor and needy speaker; Psalm 71 trusts in God from youth, asks not to be cast off in old age, and promises to declare God’s righteousness and strength to the next generation.
evidence: Read 71:5-9 and 71:17-18 and say what the speaker asks and promises.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks of God in old age in Psalm 71:9 and 71:18?

topics.name: Psalm 72: the king who judges the poor with righteousness
topics.description: The psalm prays that God give the king his judgments and righteousness so that he judges the poor, saves the needy, and breaks the oppressor, that his dominion be from sea to sea and his name endure, and all nations be blessed in him.
evidence: Read 72:1-4, 72:12-14 and 72:17-19 and list what the king does for the poor.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what kind of king Psalm 72 describes and how he treats the poor?

topics.name: Psalm 73: why the wicked prosper; I went into the sanctuary
topics.description: The speaker nearly slipped because he envied the prosperity of the wicked and thought cleansing his heart was in vain, until he went into God’s sanctuary and understood their end; he says God is the strength of his heart and his portion and it is good to draw near to God.
evidence: Read 73:1-14 and 73:15-20 and say what changed his view.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what changed the speaker’s mind in Psalm 73:16-17?

topics.name: Psalm 74: a lament over the destroyed sanctuary
topics.description: The people ask why God has cast them off for ever, describe the enemy wrecking the sanctuary and burning the meeting places, say there is no prophet, recall God’s power in creation and dividing the sea, and ask him to plead his cause.
evidence: Read 74:1-11 and 74:12-17 and say how remembering God’s past works shapes the plea.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the people recall creation and the sea in Psalm 74:12-17?

topics.name: Psalms 75-76: God is the judge; God is known in Judah
topics.description: In Psalm 75 the speaker gives thanks to God and says he judges uprightly, puts down one and sets up another, and warns the boastful; Psalm 76 says God is known in Judah, his dwelling is in Zion, and he breaks the weapons and rebukes the proud.
evidence: Read 75:6-8 and 76:1-3 and say who judges and where he is known.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 75:6-7 says about who raises and who puts down?

topics.name: Psalm 77: I will remember the works of the LORD
topics.description: In trouble the speaker cries to God and asks whether he has cast off for ever and forgotten to be gracious; then he resolves to remember the works and wonders of the LORD, who led his people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
evidence: Read 77:7-9 and 77:10-20 and trace the turn from questions to remembering.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker does in Psalm 77:10-12 when he feels God has forgotten him?

topics.name: Psalm 78: tell the coming generation what God did and how Israel rebelled
topics.description: The speaker says the fathers must teach their children the LORD’s works so they will not be stubborn like their fathers; he retells Egypt, the sea, the wilderness provision and Israel’s repeated unbelief, God’s anger, and his choosing of Judah, Zion and David.
evidence: Read 78:1-8 and say why the story is told.
Trace the cycle of provision, rebellion and judgment in 78:12-64.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the psalmist retells Israel’s history in Psalm 78:1-8 and what repeated pattern follows?

topics.name: Psalms 79-80: pleas for Jerusalem and the vine of Israel
topics.description: Psalm 79 laments that the nations have defiled God’s temple and shed blood in Jerusalem and asks God not to remember former iniquities but to help for his name’s sake; Psalm 80 prays that the Shepherd of Israel turn us again, picturing Israel as a vine brought out of Egypt.
evidence: Find the refrain in 80:3, 80:7, 80:19 and the vine imagery in 80:8-16.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the vine picture in Psalm 80 and what the people ask in the refrain?

topics.name: Psalms 81-82: hear my people; God judges among the gods
topics.description: Psalm 81 calls Israel to sing and recalls the LORD who brought them from Egypt, who asks them to listen and says he would have fed them had they obeyed; Psalm 82 shows God standing in the congregation to judge those who judge unjustly and favour the wicked.
evidence: Read 81:8-16 and 82:1-4 and say what God asks and rebukes.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what God says in Psalm 81:8-13 and what he says to the judges in Psalm 82:2-4?

topics.name: Psalm 83: a plea against nations conspiring against God’s people
topics.description: The speaker says God’s enemies make a tumult and consult together against his people, names Edom, Moab, Ammon, Assur and others, asks God to deal with them as with Midian and Sisera, so that they may know that he alone is the most high over all the earth.
evidence: Read 83:1-8 and 83:16-18 and say what the enemies plan and what the speaker asks.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the plan of the enemies in Psalm 83:3-5 and what the speaker hopes people will know?

topics.name: Psalm 84: how amiable are thy tabernacles
topics.description: The speaker longs for the courts of the LORD, says the sparrow finds a house near his altars, blesses those whose strength is in God and who pass through the valley of Baca, and says a day in his courts is better than a thousand.
evidence: Read 84:1-4 and 84:10-12 and say what the speaker values.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 84:10 says about being in God’s house?

topics.name: Psalm 85: revive us; mercy and truth meet
topics.description: The people thank the LORD for favour and forgiveness to the land, ask him to turn them again and revive them, and say mercy and truth are met together, righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
evidence: Read 85:1-7 and 85:8-13 and say what the speaker expects God to speak.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 85:10-11 says about mercy, truth, righteousness and peace?

topics.name: Psalm 86: unite my heart to fear thy name
topics.description: The speaker, poor and needy, asks the LORD to hear and preserve him, says the Lord is good and ready to forgive and there is none like him among the gods, asks to be taught his way and for a united heart, and says God is full of compassion.
evidence: Read 86:5, 86:8-11 and 86:15 and list what is said about God.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks in Psalm 86:11 and what he says about God in 86:15?

topics.name: Psalm 87: glorious things are spoken of Zion
topics.description: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob, glorious things are spoken of the city of God, and the LORD records of peoples that this one was born there.
evidence: Read 87:1-7 and list what is said about Zion and who is counted as born there.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 87 says about Zion and about the nations?

topics.name: Psalm 88: a cry from the depths with no answer in sight
topics.description: The speaker is full of troubles, near the grave, afflicted by God’s wrath and forsaken by friends, and cries to the LORD day and night; the psalm ends in darkness without a stated answer.
evidence: Read 88:1-4 and 88:13-18 and note how the psalm begins and ends.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 88 begins and why its ending is different from Psalm 13?

topics.name: Psalm 89: the LORD’s covenant with David
topics.description: The psalm sings of the LORD’s mercies and faithfulness, says he made a covenant with his chosen David and swore to establish his seed and throne for ever, then laments that the LORD has cast off and abhorred his anointed and asks him to remember.
evidence: Read 89:3-4, 89:28-37 and 89:38-45 and contrast the promise with the lament.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised David in Psalm 89 and what the psalmist complains about at the end?

topics.name: Psalm 90: teach us to number our days
topics.description: The speaker says the LORD has been our dwelling place in all generations and is God from everlasting, while man is like grass and a thousand years are as yesterday; he asks to be taught to number his days, to be satisfied with mercy, and for the work of their hands to be established.
evidence: Read 90:1-6 and 90:12-17 and contrast God’s time with man’s.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 90:12 asks God to teach and why?

topics.name: Psalm 91: he that dwells in the secret place of the most High
topics.description: The one who dwells in the secret place of the most High abides under the shadow of the Almighty, who is his refuge and fortress; he will not fear the terror by night or the arrow by day, God gives his angels charge over him, and the LORD speaks of delivering him.
evidence: Read 91:1-2 and 91:14-16 and list what the one who trusts receives.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 91:1-2 says about the person who trusts in the LORD?

topics.name: Psalms 92-93: it is good to give thanks; the LORD reigns
topics.description: Psalm 92 says it is good to give thanks to the LORD and praise his works, that the righteous flourish like a palm tree and bring forth fruit in old age; Psalm 93 declares that the LORD reigns, clothed with majesty and strength, his throne established of old.
evidence: Read 92:12-15 and 93:1-4 and say what is said about the righteous and about the LORD’s reign.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the righteous in Psalm 92:12-14 and the opening of Psalm 93?

topics.name: Psalm 94: O LORD God, to whom vengeance belongeth
topics.description: The speaker calls on God as judge of the earth to reward the proud, asks how long the wicked will triumph and kill the widow and fatherless, says the LORD who made the ear hears and he will not cast off his people, and the LORD is his defence.
evidence: Read 94:1-7 and 94:8-15 and 94:16-23 and say what the speaker asks and what he trusts.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 94:9 and 94:14?

topics.name: Psalm 95: come, let us worship; harden not your heart
topics.description: The psalm calls the people to sing to the LORD, the great King above all gods, who made the sea and dry land and is our shepherd; then it warns not to harden the heart as in the wilderness at Meribah, where God swore they should not enter his rest.
evidence: Read 95:1-7 and 95:8-11 and say what the call to worship and the warning each ask.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the two parts of Psalm 95 and what the people are warned not to do?

topics.name: Psalms 96-99: the LORD reigns over all the earth
topics.description: These psalms call the earth to sing a new song to the LORD, say all the gods of the nations are idols but the LORD made the heavens, repeat that the LORD reigns, and call the world to exalt him as holy and to rejoice at his coming to judge in righteousness.
evidence: Find the phrase “the LORD reigneth” in 96:10, 97:1 and 99:1, and say what each psalm adds.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalms 96-99 say about the LORD’s reign and the gods of the nations?

topics.name: Psalm 100: make a joyful noise unto the LORD
topics.description: All lands are called to serve the LORD with gladness, know that he made us and we are his people and the sheep of his pasture, and enter his gates with thanksgiving because he is good and his mercy is everlasting.
evidence: Read Psalm 100 and list the reasons given for thanks.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say why Psalm 100 says to give thanks to the LORD?

topics.name: Psalm 101: I will walk within my house with a perfect heart
topics.description: The speaker resolves to sing of mercy and judgment, to behave wisely in a perfect way, to set no wicked thing before his eyes, to cut off the slanderer and proud, and to look to the faithful of the land.
evidence: List the resolutions in 101:2-8.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list three things the speaker of Psalm 101 resolves to do or not to do?

topics.name: Psalm 102: the afflicted pours out his complaint; thou art the same
topics.description: The afflicted speaker says his days are consumed like smoke and his bones cleave to his skin, he is like a pelican of the wilderness and a sparrow alone, but the LORD shall endure for ever, will build up Zion and hear the destitute, and the heavens will perish while he remains.
evidence: Read 102:1-11 and 102:12-22 and 102:23-28 and contrast the speaker with the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast the speaker’s condition with the LORD’s endurance in Psalm 102?

topics.name: Psalm 103: bless the LORD, O my soul
topics.description: The speaker tells his soul to bless the LORD and forget not his benefits: forgiveness, healing, redemption; the LORD is merciful, gracious and slow to anger, removes our transgressions as far as east from west, pities like a father, and knows we are dust.
evidence: List the benefits in 103:3-5 and the character of the LORD in 103:8-14.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name some of the LORD’s benefits in Psalm 103 and read 103:8-12?

topics.name: Psalm 104: the LORD’s creation and provision
topics.description: The speaker blesses the LORD for stretching out the heavens, setting the earth’s foundations, sending springs and grass for the cattle, giving the beasts and birds their places, and says all creatures look to him for food and live when he sends his spirit.
evidence: Read 104:1-9, 104:10-23 and 104:24-30 and list what the LORD provides.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 104 says about God’s care for creation and every creature?

topics.name: Psalm 105: remember his wonderful works and his covenant with Abraham
topics.description: The psalm calls Israel to give thanks and remember the LORD’s works, recounts his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to give them Canaan, Joseph sent before them, the plagues of Egypt, and the exodus and wilderness provision, so that they might keep his statutes.
evidence: Read 105:7-11 and 105:23-45 and list the events retold.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list four events recounted in Psalm 105 and say why they are told?

topics.name: Psalm 106: our fathers sinned; he remembered his covenant
topics.description: The psalm confesses that the fathers sinned at the Red Sea, in the wilderness with the golden calf, at Baal-peor and at Meribah, and in Canaan among the heathen, yet God heard their cry and remembered his covenant; the speaker asks him to gather them from the nations.
evidence: Read 106:6-7 and 106:44-48 and list the sins confessed in 106:13-39.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 106 differs from Psalm 105 in how it tells Israel’s history?

topics.name: Psalm 107: let the redeemed of the LORD say so
topics.description: The redeemed are told to give thanks for the LORD’s goodness; four groups are described, wanderers in the wilderness, prisoners, the sick, and sailors in a storm, each cried to the LORD in trouble and he delivered them.
evidence: List the four groups and find the repeated refrain (107:8, 15, 21, 31).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name the four groups in Psalm 107 and the refrain that follows each?

topics.name: Psalm 108: awake, psaltery and harp
topics.description: The speaker resolves to sing and praise, says God’s mercy is great above the heavens, and asks for help against the enemy using words that also appear in Psalm 60:5-12 about Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah and Edom.
evidence: Compare Psalm 108:6-13 with 60:5-12 and note the shared words.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} compare Psalm 108 with Psalm 57 and Psalm 60 and say which verses are alike?

topics.name: Psalm 109: a cry against false accusers
topics.description: The speaker says the wicked speak against him with lying tongues and repay evil for love, and prays that the accuser’s days be few and his reward come from the LORD; he says he is poor and needy and asks God to save him.
evidence: Read 109:1-5, 109:6-20 and 109:21-31 and note how the psalm moves from complaint to curse to appeal.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 109 moves from the speaker’s complaint to his prayer for help?

topics.name: Psalm 110: sit at my right hand; a priest after Melchizedek
topics.description: The LORD says to the speaker’s Lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are his footstool; he is a king sent to rule from Zion and a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, sworn by the LORD.
evidence: Read 110:1-4 and say who speaks and to whom, and what is sworn.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Psalm 110:1 and 110:4 and say what the LORD says to the speaker’s Lord?

topics.name: Psalms 111-112: the works of the LORD and the blessed man who fears him
topics.description: Psalm 111 praises the LORD’s works, righteousness and covenant, saying the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; Psalm 112 describes the man who fears the LORD and delights in his commandments, whose righteousness endures and who is gracious and gives to the poor.
evidence: Read 111:10 and 112:1-9 and say what each says about the fear of the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 111:10 and Psalm 112:1 connect the fear of the LORD with wisdom and blessing?

topics.name: Psalms 113-114: the LORD lifts the poor; the sea saw it and fled
topics.description: Psalm 113 calls the LORD’s servants to praise his name, says he dwells on high yet humbles himself and raises the poor from the dust; Psalm 114 recalls Israel leaving Egypt when the sea fled and Jordan turned back and the earth trembled before the LORD.
evidence: Read 113:5-9 and 114:1-8 and say what the LORD does in each.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 113:7-8 says about the poor and what Psalm 114 recalls?

topics.name: Psalm 115: not unto us; idols and the living God
topics.description: The psalm gives glory to the LORD’s name, says the heathen’s idols have mouths that speak not and eyes that see not and those who trust them become like them, and calls Israel, the house of Aaron and all who fear him to trust the LORD, their help and shield.
evidence: Read 115:4-8 and 115:9-11 and contrast idols with the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast the idols with the LORD in Psalm 115?

topics.name: Psalm 116: I love the LORD because he heard my voice
topics.description: The speaker loves the LORD because he heard his voice, tells how the sorrows of death compassed him and he called on the LORD who delivered his soul, and asks what he can render, promising to take the cup of salvation and pay his vows in the presence of all his people.
evidence: Read 116:3-4 and 116:12-19 and say what the speaker does in thanks.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker promises to do in Psalm 116:12-14?

topics.name: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
topics.description: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
evidence: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?

topics.name: Psalm 119:1-32: blessed are those who walk in the law of the LORD
topics.description: The psalm opens by calling blessed those who walk in the LORD’s law, asks how a young man may cleanse his way and says he has hid God’s word in his heart, and asks the LORD to open his eyes to see wondrous things out of his law.
evidence: Read 119:9-11 and say how a young man is to cleanse his way.
List the different words for God’s word used in 119:1-32.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Psalm 119:9-11 and name three words the psalm uses for God’s word?

topics.name: Psalm 119:33-64: teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes
topics.description: The speaker asks the LORD to teach him his statutes, turn his eyes from vanity, and let his mercies come; he says he will speak of the LORD’s testimonies before kings, is the LORD’s portion, and has turned his feet to the LORD’s testimonies.
evidence: Pick three requests the speaker makes in 119:33-40.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list what the speaker asks God to teach and turn away in Psalm 119:33-40?

topics.name: Psalm 119:65-96: it is good for me that I have been afflicted
topics.description: The speaker says that before he was afflicted he went astray but now keeps God’s word, that it is good for him to have been afflicted that he might learn the statutes, that God’s hands made him, and that God’s word is settled for ever in heaven.
evidence: Read 119:67, 119:71, 119:75 and 119:89 and say what the speaker has learned through affliction.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 119:67 and 119:71 say about affliction?

topics.name: Psalm 119:97-128: O how I love thy law; thy word is a lamp unto my feet
topics.description: The speaker loves God’s law and meditates on it all day, says it makes him wiser than his enemies and teachers, calls God’s words sweeter than honey, and says the word is a lamp unto his feet and a light unto his path.
evidence: Read 119:97-105 and say what the speaker says the law gives him.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Psalm 119:105 and explain what it says the word does?

topics.name: Psalm 119:129-160: the entrance of thy words giveth light
topics.description: The speaker says God’s testimonies are wonderful and his words give light and understanding, weeps because others do not keep the law, asks to be redeemed from oppression, and says the sum of God’s word is truth and every righteous judgment endures for ever.
evidence: Read 119:129-136 and 119:160 and say what the speaker says about God’s word.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 119:130 and 119:160 say about God’s word?

topics.name: Psalm 119:161-176: great peace have they which love thy law
topics.description: The speaker says princes persecute him without cause but his heart stands in awe of God’s word, he rejoices at it as one who finds great spoil, praises God seven times a day, says great peace have they that love the law, and ends by asking to be sought as a lost sheep.
evidence: Read 119:161-168 and 119:176 and say how the psalm ends.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 119 ends and what the speaker asks in verse 176?

topics.name: Psalms 120-121: distress among liars; my help comes from the LORD
topics.description: Psalm 120 cries to the LORD in distress against lying lips and a deceitful tongue, among those who hate peace; Psalm 121 lifts the eyes to the hills and says help comes from the LORD who made heaven and earth and who keeps his people and never slumbers.
evidence: Read 121:1-8 and list what the LORD keeps and when.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 121 says about who keeps the speaker and when?

topics.name: Psalm 122: I was glad when they said, let us go to the house of the LORD
topics.description: The speaker is glad to go up to the house of the LORD to Jerusalem, where the tribes go up and the thrones of the house of David are set, and asks others to pray for the peace of Jerusalem.
evidence: Read 122:1-9 and list the reasons to love Jerusalem.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Psalm 122:6-9 asks and why?

topics.name: Psalms 123-125: our eyes wait upon the LORD
topics.description: Psalm 123 lifts eyes like servants watching a master’s hand and asks for mercy against contempt; Psalm 124 says that if the LORD had not been on our side the proud waters would have gone over us; Psalm 125 says those who trust in the LORD are like mount Zion, which cannot be removed.
evidence: Find the pictures in 123:2, 124:7 and 125:1-2.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain one picture each from Psalms 123, 124 and 125?

topics.name: Psalm 126: they that sow in tears shall reap in joy
topics.description: The people recall the LORD turning again the captivity of Zion when they were like those who dream, filled with laughter, and pray for the LORD to turn their captivity again, saying those who sow in tears shall reap in joy.
evidence: Read 126:5-6 and say what the sower does and receives.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the picture of sowing in tears and reaping in joy in Psalm 126:5-6?

topics.name: Psalms 127-128: unless the LORD builds the house; the blessed family
topics.description: Psalm 127 says that unless the LORD builds the house those who build it labour in vain, and that children are a heritage from the LORD; Psalm 128 blesses the one who fears the LORD with the fruit of his labour, a fruitful wife and children, and the good of Jerusalem.
evidence: Read 127:1-2 and 128:1-4 and say what depends on the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 127:1 teaches about work and the LORD?

topics.name: Psalm 129: they have afflicted me from my youth, yet have not prevailed
topics.description: Israel says they have often been afflicted from their youth yet not overcome, the LORD is righteous and has cut asunder the cords of the wicked, and those who hate Zion are compared to grass on the housetops that withers.
evidence: Read 129:1-4 and say why the afflicted have not been overcome.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 129:2-4 says about the afflicted and the LORD?

topics.name: Psalms 130-131: out of the depths; a weaned child
topics.description: Psalm 130 cries to the LORD out of the depths, says that with him there is forgiveness and plenteous redemption, and waits for him more than watchmen for the morning; Psalm 131 says the speaker is not haughty and has quieted his soul like a weaned child, and both end by telling Israel to hope in the LORD.
evidence: Read 130:3-8 and 131:1-3 and say what Israel is told to do.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 130:3-4 says about forgiveness and what 130:7 and 131:3 tell Israel to do?

topics.name: Psalm 132: the LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion
topics.description: The psalm recalls David’s vow to find a dwelling for the LORD and says the LORD swore to David that his seed would sit on his throne if his children keep his covenant; the LORD chose Zion for his rest and will make the horn of David to bud.
evidence: Read 132:11-18 and say what the LORD swore and what he chose.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 132:11-12 says the LORD swore to David?

topics.name: Psalms 133-134: brethren in unity; bless the LORD in the night
topics.description: Psalm 133 says it is good and pleasant when brethren dwell together in unity, like precious ointment and the dew of Hermon, for there the LORD commands the blessing; Psalm 134 calls the LORD’s servants who stand in his house by night to lift up their hands and bless him.
evidence: Read 133:1-3 and 134:1-3 and say who is called to do what.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 133:1 says is good and what Psalm 134 calls the servants to do?

topics.name: Psalm 135: praise the LORD who is great above all gods
topics.description: The psalm calls the LORD’s servants to praise him, says he is above all gods and does whatever he pleases in heaven and earth, recalls Egypt’s firstborn and the defeat of Sihon and Og, and says those who make idols become like them.
evidence: Read 135:5-14 and 135:15-18 and list what the LORD does and what idols are.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 135 contrasts the LORD with idols?

topics.name: Psalm 136: his mercy endureth for ever
topics.description: Each verse tells a work of the LORD, from creation of the heavens and lights to the striking of Egypt’s firstborn, the dividing of the Red Sea and the giving of the land, and each is followed by the refrain that his mercy endures for ever.
evidence: Read Psalm 136 and list the works named, noting the repeated refrain.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list three works of the LORD in Psalm 136 and say the refrain?

topics.name: Psalm 137: by the rivers of Babylon
topics.description: Exiles sit by the rivers of Babylon and weep when they remember Zion, hang up their harps when their captors ask for a song, and vow not to forget Jerusalem; the psalm ends with a plea against Babylon and Edom.
evidence: Read 137:1-6 and say what the exiles refuse to do and what they promise.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the exiles in Psalm 137 will not sing and what they vow about Jerusalem?

topics.name: Psalm 138: I will praise thee with my whole heart
topics.description: The speaker praises the LORD for his lovingkindness and truth, for answering when he cried, says kings shall sing of the LORD and that though he is high he regards the lowly, and says the LORD will perfect that which concerns him.
evidence: Read 138:1-8 and say what the speaker praises God for.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 138:6-8 about God and the lowly?

topics.name: Psalm 139: O LORD, thou hast searched me and known me
topics.description: The speaker says the LORD knows his sitting and rising and thoughts, that he cannot flee from his presence in heaven, the depths or the uttermost sea, that God formed him in the womb so that he is fearfully and wonderfully made, and asks God to search him and lead him.
evidence: Read 139:1-6, 139:7-12 and 139:13-16 and say what each part says about God.
Read 139:23-24 as a prayer.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 139 says about God’s knowledge of us and his presence?

topics.name: Psalms 140-142: deliver me from violent men; I cried unto the LORD
topics.description: Psalm 140 asks the LORD to deliver the speaker from evil and violent men whose tongues are like serpents; Psalm 141 asks that his prayer be set before the LORD like incense and that he be kept from wickedness; Psalm 142 pours out his complaint, saying the LORD is his refuge and portion.
evidence: Read 140:1-3, 141:1-4 and 142:1-7 and list what the speaker asks.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 141:2-4 and 142:5 say about the speaker’s prayer and refuge?

topics.name: Psalm 143: enter not into judgment with thy servant
topics.description: The speaker asks the LORD to hear and not to enter into judgment with him since in God’s sight no man living is righteous, remembers the days of old, spreads out his hands, and asks to be taught to do God’s will and led into the land of uprightness.
evidence: Read 143:1-2 and 143:8-10 and list what the speaker asks.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 143:2 says about being righteous in God’s sight?

topics.name: Psalm 144: blessed be the LORD my strength; happy is that people
topics.description: The speaker blesses the LORD who teaches his hands to war and is his fortress and deliverer, asks what man is that God takes knowledge of him, asks for rescue from false and strange children, and describes the happy people whose God is the LORD.
evidence: Read 144:1-4 and 144:12-15 and list the names for God and the picture of the happy people.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 144:15 says makes a people happy?

topics.name: Psalm 145: I will extol thee, my God, O King
topics.description: The speaker will bless the LORD every day and speak of his greatness, calls him gracious, full of compassion, slow to anger, good to all, near to all who call on him, upholding the fallen, and says his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom.
evidence: Read 145:8-9 and 145:13-20 and list what is said about God’s character and care.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Psalm 145:8-9 and name three things it says about the LORD?

topics.name: Psalms 146-148: praise the LORD from the heavens and the earth
topics.description: Psalm 146 says to praise the LORD all one’s life and not to trust in princes, since the LORD gives justice and feeds the hungry; Psalm 147 praises him for rebuilding Jerusalem, healing the broken-hearted and his word on the earth; Psalm 148 calls angels, the sun, moon, stars, sea creatures, mountains and kings to praise him.
evidence: List what is called to praise the LORD in Psalm 148 and what the LORD does in 146:7-9.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list five things called to praise the LORD in Psalm 148?

topics.name: Psalms 149-150: let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD
topics.description: Psalm 149 calls the saints to sing a new song to the LORD with dancing and swords in their hands; Psalm 150 closes the book by calling for praise of God in his sanctuary and firmament with trumpet, harp, cymbals and all that has breath.
evidence: Read Psalm 150 and list where, why and with what God is to be praised.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Psalm 150 and say who is to praise the LORD and with what?

topics.name: Proverbs: overview
topics.description: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
evidence: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?

topics.name: The purpose of Proverbs and the fear of the LORD
topics.description: Proverbs is given to know wisdom and instruction, to give prudence to the simple and knowledge to the young, and it names the fear of the LORD as the beginning of knowledge while fools despise wisdom.
evidence: Name what Proverbs 1:2-4 says the book is for and what 1:7 calls the beginning of knowledge.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Proverbs 1:7 and explain it in their own words?

topics.name: Do not follow sinners; wisdom cries out
topics.description: A father urges his son to hear instruction and not consent when sinners entice him to join violence; Wisdom cries in the streets and warns those who hate knowledge and refuse her reproof.
evidence: Describe the enticement of 1:10-14 and the warning of 1:24-33.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the two warnings in Proverbs 1: the sinners’ enticing and Wisdom’s rebuke?

topics.name: Seeking wisdom: protection and the right path
topics.description: The father says that if the son seeks wisdom like silver he will understand the fear of the LORD, and wisdom will deliver him from evil men and from the strange woman and keep him on the way of good men.
evidence: List what Proverbs 2 says the LORD gives and what wisdom keeps the son from.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the son must do and what he will receive in Proverbs 2?

topics.name: Trust in the LORD with all your heart
topics.description: The father tells his son to keep his commandments, trust in the LORD and not lean on his own understanding, accept the LORD’s correction, value wisdom above silver and gold, and do good to his neighbour.
evidence: Read 3:5-6 and say what the son is told to do and what the LORD does.
Find 3:11-12 and say what it says about correction.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 3:5-6 and give one example of leaning on one’s own understanding?

topics.name: Get wisdom; guard your heart
topics.description: A father recalls the teaching he received, tells his son to get wisdom and understanding, to avoid the path of the wicked, and to keep his heart with all diligence since the issues of life flow from it.
evidence: Contrast the paths in 4:14-19 and 4:18.
Say what 4:23 tells the son to guard.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain 4:23 and name the two paths described in chapter 4?

topics.name: Warnings against the strange woman
topics.description: The father warns his son against the strange woman whose lips drop honey but whose end is bitter and whose feet go down to death, and urges him to find joy in the wife of his youth.
evidence: Read Proverbs 5:3-6 and 5:15-19 and contrast the warning with the counsel.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the warning of Proverbs 5 and the counsel given in 5:15-19?

topics.name: Surety, sloth and seven abominations
topics.description: Proverbs warns against becoming surety for a neighbour, sends the sluggard to the ant, describes the froward man who sows discord, and lists six things the LORD hates, even seven.
evidence: List the six things and the seventh named in 6:16-19.
Say what the ant teaches in 6:6-8.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list some of the seven things the LORD hates in Proverbs 6:16-19?

topics.name: Keep the commandment; the snare of adultery
topics.description: The father says the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, warns that adultery brings ruin and burning that cannot be hidden, and in chapter 7 tells how a simple young man is lured by a woman and walks to her house like an ox to the slaughter.
evidence: Describe the young man’s steps in 7:6-23 and the closing warning in 7:24-27.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the scene in Proverbs 7 and the warning it ends with?

topics.name: Wisdom calls aloud and was there at creation
topics.description: Wisdom cries out to the simple, says she is better than rubies, loves those who love her, and describes herself as brought forth by the LORD before the earth and rejoicing when he set the heavens and the foundations of the earth.
evidence: Read 8:22-31 and say what Wisdom says about her place before and during creation.
List what Wisdom offers in 8:12-21.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Wisdom says about herself in Proverbs 8:22-31?

topics.name: Two invitations: Wisdom’s house and Folly’s seat
topics.description: Wisdom builds a house, prepares a feast and calls the simple to come, while a foolish woman sits at her door and calls them to stolen waters; the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the LORD.
evidence: Compare the two invitations in 9:1-6 and 9:13-18.
Read 9:10.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} compare the invitation of Wisdom and the invitation of the foolish woman in Proverbs 9?

topics.name: Proverbs of Solomon: the righteous, the wicked and words (10-11)
topics.description: Short sayings contrast the righteous and the wicked, the diligent and the lazy, and the mouth that gives life with the mouth that harms; chapter 11 adds sayings on integrity, pride, surety and generosity.
evidence: Collect three contrasts between righteous and wicked from chapter 10 and chapter 11.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} pick one saying from Proverbs 10 or 11 and explain what two ways of life it contrasts?

topics.name: Fools, counsel, truth and diligence (12-13)
