topics.description: The sayings praise truthful lips over lying tongues, the one who hears counsel over the fool who is right in his own eyes, and diligent work over slothfulness; chapter 13 speaks about the mouth, wealth and discipline.
evidence: Find a saying about speech, one about work, and one about counsel in chapters 12-13.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 12:15 and give a saying from chapters 12-13 about work?

topics.name: The fear of the LORD, the simple and the prudent (14-15)
topics.description: The sayings contrast the simple who believe every word with the prudent who consider their steps, call the fear of the LORD a fountain of life, say that oppressing the poor insults their Maker, and teach that a soft answer turns away wrath.
evidence: Read 14:27, 14:31 and 15:1 and say what each teaches.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 15:1 and give an example from daily life?

topics.name: The LORD directs; pride and strife (16-17)
topics.description: The sayings say a man’s plans are before the LORD, that pride goes before destruction, that the LORD tries hearts as a furnace tries gold, and that justifying the wicked or condemning the just is an abomination to him.
evidence: Read 16:3, 16:18 and 17:15 and state the lesson of each.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 16:18 and name one saying about the LORD’s part in human plans in chapter 16?

topics.name: The tongue, friends, anger, rich and poor (18-19)
topics.description: The sayings warn that a fool’s mouth is his destruction, that death and life are in the power of the tongue, that a brother offended is hard to win, that discretion defers anger, and that the poor are often forsaken while the fear of the LORD leads to life.
evidence: Read 18:21 and 19:11 and say what each teaches.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 18:21 in their own words?

topics.name: Honest weights, justice and the safety of the LORD (20-21)
topics.description: The sayings say wine is a mocker, that divers weights are an abomination to the LORD, that doing justice is more acceptable to him than sacrifice, and that the horse is prepared for battle but safety is of the LORD.
evidence: Read 20:23, 21:3 and 21:31 and state what each says.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 21:3 and say why it matters?

topics.name: Good name, training a child, and the poor (22:1-16)
topics.description: The sayings praise a good name over riches, say the rich and poor meet before their maker, tell parents to train up a child in his way, and say the rich rule over the poor while the borrower is servant to the lender.
evidence: Read 22:1, 22:2 and 22:6 and say what each teaches.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 22:6 and name something from 22:1-16 about the poor?

topics.name: Sayings of the wise: do not rob the poor, do not envy sinners
topics.description: The writer calls the reader to bow the ear to the words of the wise so that trust may be in the LORD, forbids robbing the poor, warns against greed for riches, correction of a child, the drunkard and the winebibber, and urges buying truth and not envying sinners.
evidence: Read 23:29-35 and describe the picture of strong drink.
Read 22:17-21 and say why the writer addresses the reader.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says is the reason for these sayings in Proverbs 22:17-21?

topics.name: More sayings of the wise: wisdom, enemies and the sluggard’s field
topics.description: The sayings say not to envy evil men, that wise men are strong, that respect of persons in judgment is not good, that one should not rejoice when an enemy falls or repay evil, and the writer learns a lesson from the field of the slothful man.
evidence: Read 24:17-18 and 24:29 and say what each commands.
Retell what the writer sees in 24:30-34.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Proverbs 24:17 and 24:29 say about enemies?

topics.name: More proverbs of Solomon: kings, neighbours and fitting words (25)
topics.description: These proverbs, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out, speak of the glory of God to conceal a thing and the honour of kings to search it out, a word fitly spoken, restraint with a neighbour, and kindness to an enemy.
evidence: Read 25:1 and say who copied these proverbs.
Find the saying about a word fitly spoken (25:11).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what 25:1 says about the source of chapters 25-29 and give one saying from chapter 25?

topics.name: Fools, sluggards and talebearers (26)
topics.description: The proverbs liken honour for a fool to a stone bound in a sling, say a fool returns to his folly as a dog to its vomit, picture the slothful turning on his bed like a door on its hinges, and say strife ceases where there is no talebearer.
evidence: Find three images used for the fool and the sluggard in chapter 26.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list two pictures Proverbs 26 uses for a fool or a sluggard?

topics.name: Friends, boasting and tending flocks (27)
topics.description: The proverbs say not to boast of tomorrow or of yourself, that open rebuke is better than secret love, that iron sharpens iron, and that a man should know the state of his flocks.
evidence: Read 27:5-6 and 27:17 and explain the lesson on friendship.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 27:17 and name one other saying about friends or boasting in chapter 27?

topics.name: Rulers, justice and confessing sin (28-29)
topics.description: The proverbs say the wicked flee when no man pursues while the righteous are bold as a lion, that confessing and forsaking sin brings mercy, that the poor and the oppressed matter to rulers, that when the righteous rule the people rejoice, and that he who trusts his own heart is a fool.
evidence: Read 28:13 and 29:2 and say what each teaches.
Contrast 28:26 with the proverbs on the fear of the LORD.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 28:13 and give one saying about rulers from chapters 28-29?

topics.name: The words of Agur
topics.description: Agur confesses he lacks understanding, asks who has ascended to heaven and gathered the wind, says every word of God is pure, asks for neither poverty nor riches, and lists things that are never satisfied or too wonderful and things that are small yet wise.
evidence: Read 30:5-9 and state what Agur asks of God.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Agur prays for in Proverbs 30:7-9?

topics.name: The words of king Lemuel
topics.description: King Lemuel recounts what his mother taught him: not to give his strength to women or to strong drink, and to open his mouth for the dumb and to plead for the poor and needy.
evidence: Read 31:8-9 and say what the king is told to do for those who cannot speak for themselves.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Lemuel’s mother tells him about kings and the poor in Proverbs 31:1-9?

topics.name: The virtuous woman
topics.description: A closing poem asks who can find a virtuous woman and describes her trust, work, care for her household and for the poor, and wise speech, concluding that a woman who fears the LORD shall be praised.
evidence: List the works and character traits of the woman in 31:10-27.
Read 31:30 and say what is praised.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the woman of Proverbs 31 and read what 31:30 says is to be praised?

topics.name: Ecclesiastes: overview
topics.description: The Preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem, examines life under the sun and declares that all is vanity, yet counsels the fear of God and keeping his commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment (12:13-14).
evidence: Say who speaks in Ecclesiastes and state the closing conclusion in 12:13-14.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the Preacher’s repeated word “vanity” and his conclusion in chapter 12?

topics.name: All is vanity: the weariness of life under the sun
topics.description: The Preacher says all is vanity, that one generation goes and another comes while the earth abides, that the sun and wind keep returning, that there is nothing new, and that he gave his heart to know wisdom and found it vexation.
evidence: Read 1:2-11 and list the cycles named.
Say what the Preacher concludes in 1:14.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what the Preacher means by “under the sun” in chapter 1?

topics.name: Pleasure, wealth and labour are vanity
topics.description: The Preacher tests pleasure, great works, gardens and riches, then sees that the wise and the fool share one event, that he must leave his labour to another, and says enjoying good in labour is from God.
evidence: List what the Preacher tried in 2:1-10 and his verdict in 2:11.
Read 2:24-26 and state what comes from the hand of God.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list what the Preacher tried in chapter 2 and what he concluded?

topics.name: A time for everything
topics.description: The Preacher says there is a season for every purpose, from birth and death to weeping and laughing, that God made everything beautiful in its time and put eternity in men’s hearts yet no man can find out his work, and that all go to the dust.
evidence: Read 3:1-8 and list four pairs.
Read 3:11 and 3:14 and say what the Preacher says about God’s work.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Ecclesiastes 3:1-8 and explain what 3:11 adds?

topics.name: Oppression, envy and two are better than one
topics.description: The Preacher sees the tears of the oppressed with no comforter, that toil arises from envy, that a man alone has no second, and that two are better than one and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
evidence: Read 4:9-12 and list the reasons two are better than one.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why two are better than one according to Ecclesiastes 4:9-12?

topics.name: Guard your step in God’s house; the vanity of riches
topics.description: The Preacher says to keep your foot when going to the house of God, not to be hasty with the mouth or with vows, and that he who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; enjoying one’s labour is a gift of God.
evidence: Read 5:1-7 and list the instructions about worship and vows.
Read 5:10-15 and state what is said about loving riches.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Ecclesiastes 5:1-7 says about speaking to God?

topics.name: Wealth without enjoyment; what is man the better?
topics.description: The Preacher describes a man to whom God gives riches but not the power to eat of them, says a stillborn child has more rest, and asks who knows what is good for man.
evidence: Say what evil the Preacher describes in 6:1-2 and what question he asks in 6:11-12.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} summarize the “evil” the Preacher sees in Ecclesiastes 6:1-2?

topics.name: Better is the house of mourning; wisdom and its limits
topics.description: The Preacher gathers sayings that the house of mourning is better than feasting, the rebuke of the wise better than the song of fools, and the end of a thing better than its beginning, notes there is not a just man who sins not, and says wisdom is far from him.
evidence: Find the “better than” sayings in chapter 7 and say what each prefers.
Read 7:20 and 7:29.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list three “better” sayings from Ecclesiastes 7 and read what 7:20 says?

topics.name: Obey the king; the work of God cannot be found out
topics.description: The Preacher counsels keeping the king’s commandment, observes that sentence against evil is not carried out speedily, that the righteous sometimes get what the wicked deserve, and that man cannot find out the work of God under the sun.
evidence: Read 8:11-14 and state what puzzles the Preacher.
Read 8:17.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what troubles the Preacher in Ecclesiastes 8:14?

topics.name: One event comes to all; enjoy life; time and chance
topics.description: The Preacher says the same event comes to the righteous and the wicked, that the living know they shall die, tells his reader to eat and drink with joy and enjoy life with the wife he loves, and says the race is not always to the swift and wisdom is better than weapons.
evidence: Read 9:7-10 and list the counsel given.
Read 9:11-12 and say what the Preacher observes.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Ecclesiastes 9:11 says about outcomes?

topics.name: Dead flies and fools: sayings on folly and wisdom
topics.description: Sayings say dead flies spoil ointment, that he who digs a pit may fall into it, that a fool is full of words, and that one should not curse the king, even in thought.
evidence: Find three sayings in chapter 10 about the fool and say what harm each describes.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain one saying about folly from Ecclesiastes 10?

topics.name: Cast your bread on the waters; remember your Creator
topics.description: The Preacher tells men to give a portion and sow in the morning since they cannot know the work of God, to rejoice in their youth yet know that God will bring them to judgment, and to remember their Creator before the evil days come.
evidence: Read 11:9-12:1 and say what is said about youth.
List the images of old age in 12:1-7.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Ecclesiastes 12:1 and explain what it tells the young to do?

topics.name: The conclusion: fear God and keep his commandments
topics.description: The Preacher sought out acceptable words, says the words of the wise are as goads and nails given by one Shepherd, warns that of making many books there is no end, and concludes that the whole duty of man is to fear God and keep his commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment.
evidence: Read 12:13-14 and state the conclusion.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} state the conclusion of Ecclesiastes in 12:13-14 in their own words?

topics.name: Song of Solomon: overview
topics.description: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s (1:1), is a poem of dialogue between a bride, her beloved and the daughters of Jerusalem, praising mutual love from first longing to its strength (8:6-7).
evidence: Name the speakers in the Song and the main settings (gardens, vineyards, the city, the wilderness).
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the speakers in the Song of Solomon and the theme of the poem?

topics.name: Longing and praise: the first meeting
topics.description: The bride longs for her beloved and speaks of him as a bundle of myrrh; he praises her as a lily among thorns, and she says she is sick of love, charging the daughters of Jerusalem not to awaken love before it pleases.
evidence: Find the speakers in 1:2-4 and 2:1-7 and list the images used for love.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} identify who is speaking in Song of Solomon 1-2:7 and what they say about each other?

topics.name: Arise, my love: the voice of the beloved in spring
topics.description: The bride hears her beloved coming over the mountains and he calls her to arise and come away because the winter is past and flowers appear; she asks for the little foxes to be caught, and says my beloved is mine and I am his.
evidence: Read 2:10-13 and list the signs of spring.
Read 2:16 and say what the bride says of the two of them.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the invitation in Song of Solomon 2:10-13 and the bride’s answer in 2:16?

topics.name: Seeking him whom my soul loves
topics.description: By night the bride seeks her beloved in the city, is found by the watchmen, and then finds him and holds him until she brings him to her mother’s house; she again charges the daughters of Jerusalem.
evidence: Retell the bride’s search in 3:1-4.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the search in Song of Solomon 3:1-4?

topics.name: Solomon’s bed and the daughters of Zion
topics.description: A procession is described coming out of the wilderness with smoke of myrrh and frankincense around the bed of Solomon with sixty valiant men, and the daughters of Zion are called to behold king Solomon with his crown on his wedding day.
evidence: Read 3:6-11 and list what is carried and who accompanies it.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the scene of 3:6-11 and name who is being looked at?

topics.name: A garden enclosed
topics.description: The beloved praises his bride at length, calls her my spouse, his garden enclosed and a spring shut up; she invites him to come into his garden, and he says he has come into his garden.
evidence: Read 4:12-5:1 and list the images of the garden and what the bride and groom say.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the garden images in Song of Solomon 4:12-5:1?

topics.name: I opened to my beloved, but he was gone
topics.description: The bride hears her beloved knocking at night, hesitates, and opens to find him gone; the watchmen strike her, and she asks the daughters of Jerusalem to tell him she is sick of love; they ask what is her beloved, and she describes him, saying he is hers.
evidence: Retell 5:2-8 and read 6:3.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the events of Song of Solomon 5:2-8 and what the bride says in 6:3?

topics.name: Praise of her beauty
topics.description: The beloved praises his bride as beautiful as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem, says there are many queens and concubines but she alone is his dove, and in chapter 7 admires her form and desires her; she says I am my beloved’s and his desire is toward me.
evidence: Find 6:8-10 and 7:10 and say what is said of the bride.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the bride says of herself and her beloved in Song of Solomon 7:10?

topics.name: Come, let us go forth into the field
topics.description: The bride invites her beloved to go forth into the field and lodge in the villages and give him her love there; she wishes he were as her brother, and charges the daughters of Jerusalem once more not to awaken love before it pleases.
evidence: Read 7:10-8:4 and list what the bride offers.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the bride invites her beloved to do in Song of Solomon 7:10-13?

topics.name: Love is strong as death
topics.description: The bride asks to be set as a seal upon his heart, saying love is strong as death and many waters cannot quench it; the closing verses speak of a little sister, Solomon’s vineyard, and the bride calling her beloved to come quickly.
evidence: Read 8:6-7 and list the images used for the strength of love.
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} read Song of Solomon 8:6-7 and explain what it says about love?
